From: Ashley Turner <ashley.turner@brightnovus.com>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: Elaine Chu <elaine.chu@brightnovus.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Apr 2028 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: QMon activation & eval integration kickoff

Hi Dylan,

Thanks for the demo last week — BrightNovus is ready to move forward with Redwood's Quality Monitoring (QMon) integration. A few priorities from our side:

- We need to onboard our initial prompt sets (clinical triage & benefits routing) and run them through an eval harness to get baseline quality metrics.
- Define regression alerting thresholds (precision/recall-style tolerances for key intents) and an automated canary that runs new model variants against a shadow traffic slice.
- Clear rollback triggers and a mute/fallback policy (we use an internal fallback that returns a safe response while ops investigates).

I've attached a short requirements workbook with sample prompts and traffic estimates (BrightNovus_qmon_requirements.xlsx). Our target is to have an initial canary + alerting enabled for the triage flow by the end of May.

Could you propose an internal plan (owners/timeline) and a short mutual action plan for the kickoff call next week? Also please advise what we should prepare on our side (log access, sample payloads, PII redaction notes).

Appreciate it —
Ashley
Director, Product Ops
BrightNovus Health

Folks — forwarding BrightNovus's kickoff request. High level: they want prompt set onboarding, eval baseline, regression alerts, canary + rollback. Timeline target: initial canary by end of May.

Proposed internal owners and first-pass plan:

- Marissa Cole (CS prompt stewardship): curate prompt sets, generate prompt variants, and own prompt-based evaluation criteria. Deliverable: curated prompt set + golden outputs (due 2028-05-03).
- Laura Bennett (Eval integration + telemetry): wire BrightNovus's payloads into our eval harness, instrument signal collection (latency, top-K outputs, confidence proxies). Deliverable: first-run eval report and dashboards (due 2028-05-10).
- Monica Patel (Rollout & canary orchestration): configure canary slice, regression alert thresholds, and rollback automation (SLOs & runbooks). Deliverable: canary MOP and rollback playbook (due 2028-05-17).
- I'll coordinate the mutual action plan with BrightNovus, validate infra needs (log access, sample payload schema), and handle milestone sign-offs.

Preliminary SLOs/threshold ideas (we'll refine with BrightNovus):
- Regression alert if intent accuracy drops > 5% vs baseline for two consecutive canary windows.
- Canary window: 2% of traffic or 1k requests/day (whichever smaller) for 48h.
- Auto-rollback if critical intent failure rate > 8% or latency P95 degrades > 50% over baseline.

Next steps: I propose a 30-min internal sync today at 11:00 PT to finalize owners and then a joint kickoff with BrightNovus tomorrow. I attached a draft MOP (qmon_initial_mop_draft.pdf) with steps I want us to review.

Thanks —
Dylan
Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Subject: QMon kickoff — mutual action plan and canary/rollback summary

Ashley / Elaine — thanks for the quick responses and for providing the requirements workbook. Recap of what we agreed internally and what we propose as the mutual action plan:

Mutual action plan (milestones):
1) Prompt set handoff (BrightNovus) — deliver anonymized/synthesized sample dataset and the list of high-risk prompts by 2028-05-01.
2) Prompt freeze + golden outputs (Redwood/Marissa) — curate stable set of ~300 prompts and produce golden outputs by 2028-05-03.
3) Eval harness onboarding (Redwood/Laura) — ingest sample payloads, run baseline eval, and surface metrics in the QMon dashboard by 2028-05-10.
4) Canary configuration (Redwood/Monica) — confirm slice size, alert thresholds, and rollback automation; produce canary MOP by 2028-05-17.
5) Canary run & decision window (Joint) — execute 48h canary (target start 2028-05-20), review results, and either promote or rollback.

Canary & rollback specifics (proposed):
- Canary slice: 2% of triage flow traffic, capped at 1k requests/day.
- Rolling windows: 12h windows for initial detection; require two consecutive windows to open an alert.
- Detection metrics: intent accuracy drop > 5% vs baseline (critical intents), unexpected entity omission rate > 7%, latency P95 degradation > 50%.
- Auto-rollback triggers: any critical intent failure rate > 8% over a 24h window OR any single-window catastrophic regression (intent accuracy drop > 12%).
- Manual hold: BrightNovus can pause canary immediately via our console controls if they observe unacceptable behavior.
- Fallback behavior: if rollback occurs, traffic shifts to pre-canary model + Redwood applies a temporary output-masking layer for any PHI-sensitive flows until root cause is identified.

Operational items we still need from BrightNovus:
- Example payloads (schema + sample) and a contact for log access (SRE).
- Confirmation on which intents are "critical" (we recommend triage acceptance, insurance verification, escalation triggers).

Deliverables attached: qmon_initial_mop_draft.pdf (internal MOP), prompt_sample_guidelines.md (prompt rubric). Link to shared drive and the HubSpot deal above.

Suggest we hold the joint kickoff on 2028-04-28 at 10:00 PT. If that works, I'll send the invite and the agenda.

Thanks —
Dylan Brooks
